newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka criticised for scrapping rights task force.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka criticised for scrapping rights task force.

text.p: The Civil Rights Movement of Sri Lanka said on Friday it was appalled by a government order to scrap the Human Rights Task Force, a group which monitored arrests and detention under the country's emergency law.
The government set up a Human Rights Commission earlier this year to take over the work of the task force which was scrapped on June 17.

"To the best of our knowledge, the commission has not yet become operative and has not built up the institutional capacity for this purpose" Suriya Wickramasinge, secretary of the movement, said in a statement.
Scrapping of the task force would leave a big gap in the mechanism available for the protection of basic human rights, she said.
The commission was set up to try to settle disputes before they go to court, advise the government on flaws in existing human rights protection laws and raise community awareness of rights issues.
The task force monitors arrests and detention under an emergency law that governs the Indian Ocean island and investigates complaints of disappearaces and abductions by security forces.
The emergency law is routinely passed each month by parliament primarily to curb rebel activities. Sri Lanka is fighting a brutal 13-year-old war with separatist Tamil guerrillas.
The government set up the task force in 1995 and the commission in 1996 after Sri Lanka was accused of serious human rights violations.
Rights groups have accused Sri Lankan security forces of human rights abuses during operations against Tamil guerrillas as well as during a brutal crackdown on a leftwing youth uprising in 1988-90.

The international human rights group Amnesty International said in April that more than 600 people were reported to have disappeared in the island's north in the past year alone, the highest number in five years.
